subject: OrchidPay integration: SDK handshake, edge fallbacks & cutover plan
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@orchidpay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: OrchidPay integration kickoff & a couple of technical clarifications

Hi Mina / Monica,

Thanks for the intro — excited to get this moving. A few quick items from our side as we prepare for the kickoff next week:

1) SDK setup: our mobile team will consume Redwood via the SDK (Node -> backend service). Can you confirm whether the SDK supports both single-tenant (dedicated) and hosted API keys the same way? We plan to start on hosted and switch to Dedicated later.

2) Endpoint migration: we currently call /v1/generate on our internal gateway. During cutover we need a pattern that avoids request duplication and preserves idempotency for ephemeral chat sessions. Any recommended routing/headers?

3) Retries / timeouts: our platform uses a default 10s request timeout and simple exponential backoff (2xx, 3 retries). For LLM calls we know token latency is variable — what are Redwood's best-practice timeout and backoff parameters for low-latency SLOs (95p < 250ms per token for short prompts)?

4) Rate limits: we have spikes during batch billing runs. Are there recommended ways to smooth bursts (client-side leaky bucket, server-side rate fencing, or suggestions around batching size)?

Practical asks: if you can share a minimal server-side snippet to wire the SDK with recommended timeouts/retry/backoff and an outline of the cutover steps (routing headers, health-checks, ramp plan) that would be great. I attached our internal API contract for reference.

Thanks — Sasha
Sasha Ivanov
Head of Integrations, OrchidPay

Attachment: orchidpay-api-contract.yaml (referenced)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@orchidpay.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrchidPay integration kickoff & a couple of technical clarifications

Hi team — adding ops/implementation detail from the runtime side and a proposed 5-step cutover plan. Pasted below are the practical defaults we use across customers running production traffic.

Recommended timeouts / retries (practical):
- Client request timeout: 30s (for non-streaming).
- Streaming: 90s read timeout, client should support connection resume if a network blip occurs.
- Retries: 2 retries on 5xx / 429 with jittered exponential backoff. For 429 prefer backoff with rate-reduction signal (do not retry immediately).
- Backoff params: initial 150ms, multiplier 2, jitter 0.25, max backoff 1200ms.

Rate limit handling & burst smoothing:
- Short-term spikes: client leaky-bucket (token bucket) with burst capacity tuned to your 99p peak.
- Server-side fencing: per-customer buckets + per-route buckets; we can set a soft-threshold and return Retry-After with quota status to the client.
- Batching: use batch size up to 8-16 for short prompts (reduces per-token cost). For chat streams, prefer incremental KV caching to avoid re-sending conversation history.

Cutover plan (5-step, recommended):
1) Mirror traffic: for 24h send a copy of requests to Redwood (no user-visible change) to validate outputs and costs.
2) Canary (1%): route 1% of traffic to Redwood endpoint; monitor latency, error rate, and output diffs.
3) Ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%): double traffic every 30–60m if metrics stable.
4) Observe/rollback window: maintain 60–90m observation window after each stage. Automatic fallback to previous provider on error threshold.
5) Finalize & rotate keys: after 100% stable, rotate keys and cut the mirror.

Routing headers and idempotency: send X-Client-Session, Idempotency-Key, X-Origin-Gateway: orchidpay-gw. For rollbacks, we recommend a transparent header X-Redwood-Mirror: true so we can annotate logs without affecting responses.

Attached: retry-matrix.csv (example error codes, recommended action), and we've added an internal Drive runbook link in related_links.

If you want, we can run a 30m technical run-through before the kickoff to walk the devs through the sample-snippets and the leaky-bucket helper.

— Vivek
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina / Vivek — this is perfect and exactly the level of detail we need. A couple quick notes from our infra lead:

- We will adopt the 30s timeout for non-streaming and implement the leaky-bucket with burst tokens = 200 for our peak window.
- For idempotency we will include Idempotency-Key for all stateful chat updates.
- Proposed kickoff: Tue Mar 28, 10:00 PT — 30m technical walk-through (dev + infra). Can you send a calendar invite?

Also please share the DocuSign link for the Dedicated addendum and the HubSpot deal link so our procurement team can accelerate.

We reviewed the sample-snippets.zip and see the batching helper — we'll test locally and share any edge cases.

Best,
